title: Isandro and the Escarpment
premise: Elodie Yarrow leads a small crew of desert rangers who survive by staying off every map and out of every ledger, tracking petty thieves across the Escarpment for whoever can pay in water and silence. When her old rival Sable Vane hires them to escort a survey team up the river that carved the Escarpment—river whose source lies inside the Concession, land sworn off after a massacre the crew's founding members helped cover up—the job collides with the one secret that holds their found family together. As permits expire and the crew's youngest member, Isandro, discovers his own birth is tangled in the massacre, Elodie must choose between keeping the crew invisible and giving the dead of the Concession their names back. They reach the forbidden source, expose the concession's forged permits to the last honest magistrate, and end the book scattered but unbroken: Elodie walks into exile with her name spoken aloud for the first time, while Isandro stays to help the river towns rebuild.
about_author: Mirabel Ishikawa spent six years as a hydrology field technician before turning to fiction, and her novels are known for landscapes that behave like characters with grudges. She writes from a converted water station on the edge of a dry lakebed, where she keeps meticulous journals of weather she refuses to romanticize.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Elodie Yarrow tracks a horse thief across the salt flats, only to find the 'thief' is a starving boy, Isandro, stealing water not horses. Her POV establishes the ranger code: take nothing you can't carry, leave no name behind. The emotional beat is weary mercy—she takes him on as a tracker's apprentice instead of turning him out.

chapters.title: Crew of No Names
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV introduces the crew at their hidden camp: quartermaster Bex, demolitions expert Ovid, medic Tamsin, and scout Ferro. Each has erased their past; Isandro is the only one allowed none. The beat is warmth inside secrecy—he belongs, as long as he never asks where anyone came from.

chapters.title: Water Ledger
chapters.summary: Bex's POV: the crew runs its books at a waystation, trading route knowledge to caravans. A courier arrives with a sealed offer from Sable Vane. Elodie burns it unread, and the beat is dread—everyone notices her hands shake, the first crack in the captain's composure.

chapters.title: The Rival's Terms
chapters.summary: Sable Vane appears in person at a border town saloon, all charm and old grievances. Through Elodie's POV we learn they once worked together and parted over something unsaid. The offer: escort a survey team up the River Anselm to the Concession line. The beat is temptation wrapped in insult.

chapters.title: Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV reveals why the Concession is taboo: twenty years ago, miners there were massacred, and the crew's founders carried the paperwork that made it look legal. The vote splits three-two. The beat is grief resurfacing—old wounds don't scar, they just wait.

chapters.title: Permits and Deadlines
chapters.summary: Ovid's POV examines the concession permits Vane's employers hold: ninety days until expiry, after which the government reverts the land. Whoever controls the source controls the water rights for a hundred miles. The beat is cold arithmetic—someone intends to own a river.

chapters.title: Hiring On
chapters.summary: Elodie signs the contract with a private clause: the crew goes armed and answers to no surveyor. Isandro's POV watches her sign and reads it as betrayal of everything he was taught. The beat is disillusionment—the hero's code bends the moment money appears.

chapters.title: The Survey Team
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV meets the clients: a nervous junior engineer, Pell, and a hard-eyed company man, Dreele, plus twelve porters. Ferro counts weapons instead of gear and doesn't like the ratio. The beat is suspicion—the job smells wrong in ways no permit explains.

chapters.title: First Water
chapters.summary: The expedition enters the canyon country. Elodie's POV teaches Isandro how to read the river's moods—green foam means flash flood upstream. The beat is mentorship deepening even as trust frays; the desert becomes a character with opinions.

chapters.title: Old Tracks
chapters.summary: Isandro finds a rusted mining cart rail half-buried in sand—evidence of the old Concession road everyone pretends doesn't exist. His POV: he asks Tamsin about the massacre and gets silence. The beat is the first stone of the mystery laid in his hands.

chapters.title: Dreele's Map
chapters.summary: Ovid lifts a copy of Dreele's route map and finds marked sites that aren't geological: cairns, a burned homestead, a mass grave symbol. His POV delivers the beat of quiet horror—the survey is a search for bodies, or for proof they never existed.

chapters.title: The Burned Homestead
chapters.summary: At a charred ruin, Pell confides in Isandro that the company hired them to 'document nothing'—to erase remaining evidence before the permits lapse. Isandro's POV: the beat is moral vertigo, a boy realizing his employers are arsonists of history.

chapters.title: Flash Flood
chapters.summary: A storm sends a wall of water down the slot canyon. Elodie's POV drives the survival sequence; two porters drown despite everything. The beat is fury and guilt—Elodie knew the signs and misjudged by an hour, and the crew sees her doubt herself for the first time.

chapters.title: Burial Without Names
chapters.summary: Tamsin buries the porters under stones with no markers, per ranger custom. Her POV contrasts the crew's namelessness with the dead who deserve names. The beat is mourning sharpening into resolve: if names matter, someone owes the Concession dead theirs.

chapters.title: Vane Follows
chapters.summary: Ferro spots a second party shadowing them—Sable Vane with hired guns, moving fast and light. Elodie's POV realizes Vane never intended the crew to finish; they're witnesses to be managed. The beat is paranoia tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Vane's men hit the camp at dawn. Ovid's POV choreographs the fight; the crew wins ugly, losing a porter and most of their pack animals. The beat is rage—Elodie captures one gunman who says only: 'She wants the ledger.'

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Interrogation scene through Elodie's POV: the gunman reveals Vane seeks a ledger kept by the massacre's paymaster—a list of names, bribes, and signatures, hidden upstream. Among the signatories, rumor says, is a name Elodie knows. The beat is dread made specific.

chapters.title: What Elodie Signed
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Elodie's POV: twenty years ago, young ranger Elodie carried a reclassification document through the Concession, believing it was boundary paperwork. She learns now what it enabled. The beat is self-recognition as complicit—her invisibility was bought with someone else's erasure.

chapters.title: Mutiny Weather
chapters.summary: Dreele orders the party onward faster; Bex refuses to move porters through dehydration risk. Bex's POV frames the standoff as the crew's code versus the company's clock. The beat is fracture—Pell and three porters side with the crew, splitting the expedition.

chapters.title: The Split Party
chapters.summary: Two camps form at the fork of the river: Dreele's downstream, the crew's upstream. Isandro's POV navigates loyalty between Elodie and the boy-porters who look to him. The beat is reluctant leadership—Isandro stops being an apprentice.

chapters.title: Cairn Field
chapters.summary: The upstream party reaches hundreds of stone cairns—unmarked graves of the massacred miners. Tamsin's POV catalogs them against the stolen map. The beat is solemnity curdling into purpose: this is why they were hired, to let the graves stay anonymous.

chapters.title: Dreele's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dreele comes upstream alone, offering Elodie triple pay and amnesty to turn back and forget. Elodie's POV plays the negotiation cool while planning otherwise. The beat is poker-faced defiance—she lets him believe greed still moves her.

chapters.title: Vane Catches Up
chapters.summary: Sable Vane confronts Elodie at the grave field, alone, and finally speaks the unsaid thing: they both ran from the Concession, but only one of them profited from running. Vane's hired guns hold the porters hostage. The beat is the rival revealed as mirror.

chapters.title: Hostages
chapters.summary: With porters at gunpoint, Vane demands the crew locate the paymaster's cache—she needs the ledger destroyed because her signature is in it too. Isandro's POV volunteers as go-between. The beat is courage without armor—a boy walking into a gun line.

chapters.title: The Paymaster's Cave
chapters.summary: Following the map's final symbols, Ovid and Isandro find a sealed cave above the river: the paymaster's strongbox, ledger intact, along with letters proving the massacre was ordered to clear the water rights. Ovid's POV: the beat is awe and horror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Reading the Dead
chapters.summary: Tamsin reads the ledger aloud by lamplight: two hundred names, payments, and the magistrate who signed the cover-up—the same magistrate now renewing the concession. Elodie's POV finds her own forged signature. The beat is devastation transfigured into evidence.

chapters.title: Permits Expire
chapters.summary: Ninety days lapse; word arrives via pigeon that the concession reverts to the crown in a week, after which the company will burn the canyon clean. Dreele's POV shows him receiving orders to expedite destruction. The beat is the clock becoming the antagonist.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Camp
chapters.summary: One of the porters, bought by Dreele, steals the ledger and bolts downstream. Ferro's POV runs the pursuit through night terrain. The beat is heartbreak—betrayal from within the small family they'd built on the river.

chapters.title: Recovery
chapters.summary: Ferro catches the thief at the falls but the ledger pages scatter into the current; Isandro dives and saves the core bundle at cost of nearly drowning. Elodie's POV pulls him out. The beat is terror and tenderness—Elodie admits aloud that Isandro is hers to protect.

chapters.title: Vane's Choice
chapters.summary: Cornered by converging company guns, Vane must burn the ledger or help the crew. In a rain-soaked parley, Elodie offers her the thing she actually wants: her name struck from the record in exchange for testimony. Vane's POV (first time): the beat is a rival choosing redemption at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Downstream Run
chapters.summary: The whole party races the company demolition team downriver, rafting the flooded gorge toward the magistrate's seat. Ovid's POV delivers the set-piece action: rapids, gunfire, and the demolition charges left behind. The beat is momentum—everything converging.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: They reach the river's true source: a spring inside the Concession, fenced and claimed, feeding the whole region. Elodie's POV stands where the massacre began. The beat is arrival and reckoning—the forbidden place is just water, and water belongs to no permit.

chapters.title: The Magistrate
chapters.summary: In the river town of Corrow, the crew presents ledger, maps, and living witnesses—including Pell—to Magistrate Halloway, son of the signing magistrate. His POV wrestles his father's legacy. The beat is justice outside the law being offered a chance to become law.

chapters.title: Company Guns at Corrow
chapters.summary: Dreele's remaining men attempt to seize the courthouse and burn the evidence. The crew, townsfolk, and defecting porters defend it in a desperate night action. Isandro's POV fights for the first time not to survive but for something. The beat is the found family weaponized for the dead.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: At dawn, Halloway voids the concession and reads all two hundred names of the massacred into the public record. Tamsin's POV watches strangers weep for people they never met. The beat is catharsis—erasure undone by the simple act of speech.

chapters.title: Costs
chapters.summary: Aftermath: Vane accepts exile rather than trial, Dreele flees and is hunted by his own company, and Elodie's forged signature means she cannot stay. Elodie's POV settles accounts with each crew member. The beat is bittersweet accounting—justice has a price and she pays it willingly.

chapters.title: What Isandro Keeps
chapters.summary: Isandro chooses to remain in Corrow as the river towns' new ranger-in-training under Halloway's protection, the first crew member to take a public name. His POV says goodbye to each mentor. The beat is growing up—the apprentice outgrowing the wilderness that raised him.

chapters.title: Exile Road
chapters.summary: Elodie walks out of the Escarpment alone at first light, name spoken freely for the first time in twenty years. Her POV passes the cairn field and leaves a marker stone. The beat is release—invisibility traded for integrity, solitude accepted without bitterness.

chapters.title: The River Remembers
chapters.summary: Final chapter braids POVs: Bex, Ovid, Tamsin, and Ferro regroup at the old camp, changed; a letter arrives from Isandro describing spring floods; far off, Elodie reads it on some other road. The beat is continuation—the crew survives, scattered but bound, and the river carries every name at last.
